_readme: Copy to brands/<slug>.seo.json and fill every field from pulls, not from memory. preview.py picks it up when brands/<slug>.audit.json also exists.

Sources, in order: seo_audit.py live (every sitemap URL), Semrush domain_rank / domain_organic / domain_organic_unique / domain_organic_organic / backlinks_overview / backlinks_refdomains for the client and each real competitor,

phrase_organic or firecrawl_search for six to eight buyer queries fetched from the client's city, phrase_related and phrase_questions per service line, the live robots.txt, sitemap and llms.txt, and the brand + reviews query.
Write 'not pulled' where a pull was not made. Never estimate a number. No em dashes, no exclamation marks, no response-time or pricing promises.

hero.heading: Where <domain> stands, and what it is worth to fix
hero.intro: Every number here came from a Semrush or Firecrawl pull or from the live HTML of the site. Where a pull was not made, the table says so. This is the baseline the engagement is measured against at 30, 60 and 90 days.
tiles: organic visits a month, <n> percent landing on the home page

findings.title: <what is missing where the buyer asks>
findings.evidence: <the ten results, named; the client's position or absence>
findings.cost: <the term volume and the AI answers that route elsewhere>
findings.fix: <what the build does, or which day of the plan>

compare.intro: The same money page at the client and at the competitors that hold the results.
rows: Google rating shown in the result
compare.verdict: <one paragraph: what the client tells engines, what competitors tell them, whether the gap is pages or links>

entity.heading: What connects the company across the web

opportunities.intro: Volume from Semrush's US database; difficulty where it was pulled.

aeo.intro: Live results for the questions a buyer types, fetched <date> from <city>. Presence here is the answer-engine scoreboard.

local: <each review platform: rating, count, position for the brand query>
plan: Reads against this baseline. The same report, re-run.
measure: Top-100 and top-10 rankings for the target terms
Average above 85 at launch and holding

hub.heading: Where you stand in search today, and what changes
hub.intro: Measured before we touched anything, so the work can be judged against it.
hub.note: Rankings or traffic. Those depend on the market and on what you publish after launch. What we promise is that nothing about the build is the reason they do not come, that every number above is re-measured at 30, 60 and 90 days, and that you see the same report we do.

sitewide: Served over HTTPS with one canonical host
robots.txt allows Google and all four AI crawlers
FAQPage schema anywhere on the site
Service schema on any service page
